title: Prime protocol code must be open source while the financial strategies that drive it stay closed
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.5.2 states that "All components of code that form part of the Prime Protocols (i.e. Spark and Grove) will be open source." A.2.8.2.2.2.5.3 immediately qualifies the scope: "The financial strategies implemented by the Prime Foundations... will be closed source," and A.2.8.2.2.2.5.3.1 assigns the Foundation "ownership of the code and strategies that determine how capital is allocated for its Prime."

The line is drawn between mechanism and judgment. The protocol is infrastructure users must be able to verify before entrusting funds to it — its correctness is a public safety property and secrecy buys nothing. The strategy is a competitive position whose value depends entirely on others not replicating it.

This is the same division the Support Scope makes elsewhere in permitting Primes to operationalize Allocation Instances "using internal, proprietary strategies that are not defined in their Artifacts." Twice, in different documents, the Atlas concludes that allocation strategy is the one thing that stays private.

What makes the closed half tolerable is that it is bounded by verifiable rails on both sides. The code that executes is public; the limits within which any strategy must operate are in the Artifact and the rate limits; and A.2.8.2.2.2.5.3.3 puts a compliance review between the strategy and the money.

The residual asymmetry is that outsiders can verify what a Prime *can* do but not what it is *doing*, so evaluating a Prime's risk-taking depends on disclosed outcomes and the ecosystem's own monitoring rather than on inspection.
description: All components of the Spark and Grove protocols are open source, yet the Foundations' capital allocation strategies are explicitly closed source and owned by the Foundation.
